title: Projective cofibrancy of the enriched free bar diagonal
statement:
Use small simplicial categories of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], simplicial sets and the simplex category of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], and enriched projective model structures of [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]. Fix one universe for all object sets and simplicial sets. Let $A$ be any small simplicial category and $X:A\to\mathsf{sSet}$ an enriched functor. Define a simplicial object $P_\bullet X$ in enriched covariant $A$-modules by
$$P_nX(b)=\coprod_{a_0,\ldots,a_n}X(a_0)\times A(a_0,a_1)\times\cdots\times A(a_{n-1},a_n)\times A(a_n,b).$$
The action in $b$ postcomposes the last factor. For $n\geq1$, the first face applies the $X$-action, an interior face composes the corresponding adjacent mapping factors, and the last face composes the final two mapping factors. Degeneracies insert an identity between the displayed vertices $a_i$ (including the last vertex $a_n$). These operators commute with the internal simplicial operators. Let $Q_AX$ be its objectwise diagonal, so
$$(Q_AX(b))_r=(P_rX(b))_r.$$
Equivalently $Q_AX=\int^{[n]\in\Delta}P_nX\times\Delta^n$, with the quotient imposing $(P(\alpha)z,t)\sim(z,\alpha t)$ for every simplex operator $\alpha$ and compatible $z,t$. Then $Q_AX$ is projectively cofibrant as an enriched $A$-module. The assertion holds for arbitrary $X$, including empty values, and does not require the mapping simplicial sets of $A$ to be Kan.

source.place: Agent-formulated enriched version of the forward free resolution in Proposition 9.11 and Remark 9.12 (printed pp.37-38), with simplicial tensors from Section 19.1 (p.90) and enriched free projective cells from HTT A.3.3.2 and Remark A.3.3.5 (pp.870-871). This is not claimed to be a numbered enriched theorem of Dugger. Archival sources WANTED. No Stacks tag supplies this enriched homotopy-theoretic assertion.

proof.text:
Work in the simplicial projective model category $\mathcal M=\mathsf{sSet}^A$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus], applied to $\mathcal A=\mathsf{sSet}$ with the Kan model structure, which is combinatorial and simplicial for its Cartesian enrichment by [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model]; tensors are objectwise. Put $F_aK(b)=K\times A(a,b)$, the free module left adjoint to evaluation at $a$. Define
$$K_n(a)=\coprod_{a_0,\ldots,a_{n-1},\,a_n=a}X(a_0)\times\prod_{j=1}^n A(a_{j-1},a_j),$$
so $K_0(a)=X(a)$ and $P_nX=\coprod_a F_aK_n(a)$. The displayed faces and degeneracies define a simplicial object: disjoint compositions or insertions commute, adjacent compositions agree by associativity, and composing an inserted identity gives the original factor by the unit law; the first-face versions are exactly the action axioms for $X$. They are enriched natural in $b$ by associativity on the final factor. Since composition, actions and identity maps are simplicial, all these operators commute with the internal operators.

source.place: Proposition 9.11 and Remark 9.12, printed pp.37–38, and §19.1, printed p.90; agent-written enriched latching calculation, not a numbered enriched theorem in this source.

proof.text: For $n>0$, let $D_n(a)\subseteq K_n(a)$ be the union of the $n$ loci where, for at least one $1\leq j\leq n$, $a_{j-1}=a_j$ and the $j$th arrow is the identity simplex; set $D_0(a)=\varnothing$. Identity simplices are preserved by every internal operator, so these are simplicial subsets. At each internal degree $r$, a bar degeneracy inserts precisely one such identity arrow, without changing the final vertex or $x\in X(a_0)_r$. The image of the iterated degeneracy indexed by a proper surjection $[n]\twoheadrightarrow[k]$ is exactly the locus of identities at its collapsed adjacent positions; deleting those positions recovers its unique preimage. The intersection of two such images imposes the union of their identity conditions and is the image obtained by deleting that union. Thus any two presentations of the same element are identified in the latching diagram: both arise from the presentation obtained by deleting the union of their collapsed positions. Conversely every diagram relation preserves the resulting element. Consequently the colimit of the coefficient degeneracy diagram ending at $a$ is exactly $D_n(a)$, and its map into $K_n(a)$ is the inclusion. This also covers $n=0$, whose latching diagram is empty.

source.place: Proposition 9.11 and Remark 9.12, printed pp.37–38, and §19.1, printed p.90; agent-written enriched latching calculation, not a numbered enriched theorem in this source.

proof.text:
All degeneracies preserve the final vertex $a$ and the final free factor $A(a,b)$. Therefore the preceding calculation gives, as a map of enriched modules,
$$L_n(P_\bullet X)\longrightarrow P_nX\;=\;\coprod_a\bigl(F_aD_n(a)\longrightarrow F_aK_n(a)\bigr).$$
Here the equality denotes an isomorphism of arrows. To check the asserted latching universal property, maps from each free summand into an arbitrary module $Z$ correspond, by the free/evaluation adjunction, to simplicial maps of its coefficient into $Z(a)$. Compatible maps on the degeneracy diagram are precisely maps $D_n(a)\to Z(a)$ by step 2; taking the family over $a$ gives exactly maps $\coprod_a F_aD_n(a)\to Z$. This proves the colimit assertion in the enriched-module category without assuming that evaluation detects projective cofibrations.

source.place: Proposition 9.11 and Remark 9.12, printed pp.37–38, and §19.1, printed p.90; agent-written enriched latching calculation, not a numbered enriched theorem in this source.

proof.text: Each inclusion $D_n(a)\hookrightarrow K_n(a)$ is a Kan-model cofibration by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. For an objectwise trivial fibration $E\to H$ of modules, a lifting square against $F_aD_n(a)\to F_aK_n(a)$ is, by the adjunction, a square against $D_n(a)\hookrightarrow K_n(a)$ and $E(a)\to H(a)$. It has a lift. A square against the coproduct is the family of these squares; choose their lifts and assemble them by the coproduct property. Hence the latching map of step 3 has the left lifting property against every projective trivial fibration, so is a projective cofibration. The Reedy criterion of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] now shows that $P_\bullet X$ is Reedy cofibrant in $\mathcal M$. In degree zero this says directly that $\coprod_aF_aX(a)$ is cofibrant, since $\varnothing\hookrightarrow X(a)$ is a cofibration for every simplicial set.

source.place: Proposition 9.11 and Remark 9.12, printed pp.37–38, and §19.1, printed p.90; agent-written enriched latching calculation, not a numbered enriched theorem in this source.

proof.text:
Apply the cofibrancy clause of [lem-coef-reedy-realization-prism] in the simplicial model category $\mathcal M$ to the Reedy-cofibrant object of step 4 (one can take its second Reedy-cofibrant object equal to the first). Its tensor realization
$$|P_\bullet X|=\int^{[n]\in\Delta}P_nX\times\Delta^n$$
is projectively cofibrant. Completeness, cocompleteness and the simplicial projective structure needed here are provided by [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus], whose hypothesis on $\mathsf{sSet}$ is [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model]; no fibrancy of $X$ or of the mapping simplicial sets has been used.

source.place: Proposition 9.11 and Remark 9.12, printed pp.37–38, and §19.1, printed p.90; agent-written enriched latching calculation, not a numbered enriched theorem in this source.

proof.text: Identify this realization with the diagonal explicitly. At an object $b$ and internal degree $r$, its elements are classes of pairs $(z,\alpha)$ with $z\in(P_nX(b))_r$ and $\alpha:[r]\to[n]$. Send this pair to $P(\alpha)z\in(P_rX(b))_r$, where $P(\alpha)$ acts in the outer direction. The coend relation makes this well-defined, since $P(\alpha)P(\beta)=P(\beta\alpha)$ when the maps are composable. Its inverse sends $w$ to $[w,1_{[r]}]$; the same relation gives $[z,\alpha]=[P(\alpha)z,1_{[r]}]$. For $\theta:[s]\to[r]$, the internal operator sends $(z,\alpha)$ to $(z|_\theta,\alpha\theta)$, whose image is $P(\alpha\theta)(z|_\theta)$. This is the diagonal operator applied to $P(\alpha)z$, because the two simplicial directions commute. The maps are enriched $A$-natural: the action by $u\in A(b,c)_r$ commutes with $P(\alpha)$ and the inverse leaves the final factor untouched. Thus this is an isomorphism of enriched modules $|P_\bullet X|\cong Q_AX$. Cofibrancy transfers across this isomorphism by the lifting definition. Empty $X(a)$ give empty summands throughout, and for $A$ empty every coproduct and latching object is initial. These cases require no change to the proof.
